newsitem.title: ITALY: Alleanza 1996 net profits rise 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: Alleanza 1996 net profits rise 60 pct.

text.p: Italian life insurance company Alleanza Assicurazioni said on Monday its 1996 net consolidated income rose 60 percent to 246.7 billion lire from 1995's figure of 154.2 billion lire.
Premium and related income rose to 3.345 trillion lire, up 12 percent from 1995's 2.987 trillion lire, of which premiums from new policies amounted to 792 billion lire.

Alleanza is Italy's largest life insurer for individual policies with a market share in Italy of 11.7 percent, and the group is 64 percent controlled by Italy's largest overall insurance company Generali.

During the first three months of 1997, net premium income from new policies amounted to 281.4 billion lire, a rise of 35.3 percent compared to the same period in 1996, while gross premium rose 21 percent to 979.4 billion lire.
"We are very pleased with these results and with our company's performance in the first three months of this year," said the group's chairman Alfonso Desiata in a statement.

"We have established ourselves as the leading company in a competitive market, and we are continuing to build business from existing and new customers. We continue to keep a firm focus on costs, which is fundamental to the success of our business," he added.
